title: Voluntary Housing Refund
description: Allows you to return any CPF savings used for your home purchase to your CPF account while still owning your property. Doing so reduces the refund amount you would have to make and increases the cash proceeds you would get when you eventually sell or transfer your property. This also boosts your retirement savings as you can benefit from CPF interest rates.
highlights: Grow your retirement savings with CPF interest rates
Greater cash proceeds and lower required CPF refund upon property sale or transfer

sections.About this support:
- Receive more cash proceeds and refund less to your CPF account when selling or transferring your property
- Take advantage of CPF’s interest rates and retire with more
- Re-use CPF savings for the various CPF approved schemes if needed
sections.Who is this for?:
- You have used your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to purchase your property
- Please note the following conditions when making the voluntary housing refund:
  - You can refund up to the CPF principal amount withdrawn towards the property plus its accrued interest to your CPF account
  - If you are an undischarged bankrupt, you have to obtain the Official Assignee’s approval to make this housing refund
  - While housing grants will generally be refunded to your OA if you have an HDB flat, the grant(s) may be partially credited to your Special Account / Retirement Account and MediSave Account if you have received more than $30,000 in grant(s)
  - If you are 55 and above, the refunded amount [will be used to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS)](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/VHRAge55), which supports your retirement needs through monthly payouts
  - Any refunds beyond your cohort’s FRS will remain in your OA
- You can read more on [housing refunds and their processes](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/sales-proceeds-after-selling-your-home)
sections.How to apply?:
Check the amount of voluntary refund you can make under the “What happens if” section in your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard).

You can make the voluntary housing refund through the following methods:

- Log in to [my cpf digital services](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/make-a-voluntary-housing-refund) using your Singpass:
  - Choose your property and enter a refund amount

Or

- Use the CPF Mobile app:
  - Download the CPF Mobile app
  - Log in with your Singpass
  - Tap on 'Services'
  - Choose 'Voluntary Housing Refund'
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only
sections.Phone number:
CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: Silver Housing Bonus (SHB)
description: Seniors aged 55 or above may receive cash bonus when they right-size to a 3-room or smaller HDB flat, and top-up the proceeds from the sale of their existing property into their CPF Retirement Account (RA) and join CPF LIFE.
highlights: Receive CPF monthly payouts for as long as they live, under CPF LIFE
Application must be submitted within 1 year from date of completion of the second housing transaction

sections.About this support:
- With effect from 1 December 2025, the SHB has been enhanced to provide greater support to seniors.
- Seniors can supplement their retirement income if they right-size from a HDB flat or private residential property with an Annual Value (AV) up to $31,000 and buy a 3-room or smaller HDB flat.
- Seniors who commit to a net increase of up to $60,000* in their CPF RA after right-sizing, with the sum going towards their retirement payouts, can qualify for an SHB amount of $30,000. They can do so using their CPF housing refunds**, if sufficient, and may no longer need to make the top-up in cash.
- They can qualify for an additional $10,000 cash bonus if they right-size to a 2-room or smaller flat, including a Community Care Apartment (CCA). This additional $10,000 bonus applies regardless of the amount they commit to their CPF RA.
- Overall, the maximum SHB amount that eligible seniors may receive is $40,000. Visit [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/retirement-planning/monetising-flat-for-retirement/silver-housing-bonus) for more details

* The net increase to commit in your CPF RA depends on the net sale proceeds and is capped at $60,000 per household. It is further capped by the prevailing Full Retirement Sum (FRS).

** CPF principal amount withdrawn to purchase a property and the accrued interest that needs to be refunded after selling the property.
sections.Who is this for?:
- At least 1 owner must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- The SC is aged 55 or above
- Monthly household income not more than $16,000
- Existing property is an HDB flat (met minimum occupation period for resale flat), or a private residential property with an Annual Value of up to $31,000
- No concurrent ownership or interest in a private residential property or in more than 1 non-residential property

Other conditions:

- Next property you are buying is a 3-room (excluding 3-room terrace) or smaller flat from HDB or from the resale market
- You must have positive net sale proceeds
- Booking of new HDB flat or application to buy resale flat must either be before sale of existing residential property, or within 12 months of completing the sale of the existing residential property
- SHB application must be submitted within 1 year from the legal completion date of the second housing transaction (either the purchase or sale)
sections.How to apply?:
- Learn about your eligibility for this scheme (and other housing monetisation options) and the estimated monthly payouts you can receive via [HDB’s 'Check Housing Monetisation Option' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR05AWEnquireHMOptions)
- To apply:
  - Enquire with our Customer Relations Executive during the appointment for second housing transaction (either resale completion or new flat keys collection appointment)
  - HDB will then schedule a financial counselling session where all the details and information such as the CPF top-up amount, bonus and the monthly payout amount would be shared during the session

title: Budget 2026 CPF Top-Up
description: Provides additional support to boost the retirement adequacy of eligible Singaporeans with CPF retirement savings below prevailing Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) through a CPF top-up in 2026.
highlights: Eligible seniors can receive up to $1,500 in CPF top-up
No application needed - eligibility will be automatically assessed

sections.About this support: $500 to $1,500 in CPF top-up for eligible Singaporean seniors, tiered by CPF retirement savings and Annual Value of the place of residence
sections.Who is this for?:
**Eligibility criteria**

- Singapore Citizen
- 50 years old and above in 2026
- CPF LIFE/Retirement Account or Ordinary/Special Account balances below prevailing BRS in 2026 of $110,200 as at 31 December 2025
- Tiered by annual value of the place of residence (as indicated on NRIC), as at 31 December 2025
- Does not own more than 1 property
sections.How to apply?: No application needed – eligibility will be automatically assessed

title: Majulah Package – Retirement Savings Bonus
description: One-off bonus for seniors with CPF retirement savings below the 2023 Basic Retirement Sum.
highlights: Eligible seniors can receive $1,000 or $1,500 one-off CPF bonus
No application needed

sections.About this support: $1,000 or $1,500 one-off Retirement Savings bonus given in December 2024, tiered by CPF retirement savings.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Born in 1973 or earlier
- Singapore Citizen residing in Singapore
- CPF retirement savings below the 2023 Basic Retirement Sum of $99,400
  - CPF retirement savings refers to the sum of Retirement Account (RA) and CPF LIFE account balances, or the sum of Ordinary Account and Special Account balances if RA has not yet been created
- Lives in a property with an Annual Value of up to $25,000
- Does not own more than 1 property
sections.How to apply?: No application required.

title: Majulah Package – Earn and Save Bonus
description: Supplements eligible working seniors' retirement savings through an annual Earn and Save Bonus credited to their CPF account.
highlights: Eligible working seniors can receive up to $1,000 annual Earn and Save Bonus in their CPF account
Bonus will be credited in March each year
No application needed

sections.About this support:
- Eligible working seniors can receive $400 to $1,000 annual Earn and Save Bonus in their CPF account, tiered by income
- Eligible working seniors with lower income will receive a higher Earn and Save Bonus
sections.Who is this for?:
**Eligibility criteria**

- Born in 1973 or earlier
- Singapore Citizen residing in Singapore
- Employed, self-employed, and/or platform worker
- Average monthly income in preceding Year of Assessment of $500 to $6,000
- Annual Value of the place of residence (as indicated on NRIC) must not exceed $31,000, as at 30 November of the preceding year
- Does not own more than 1 property
sections.How to apply?:
**Employees and Platform Workers**

- No application required
- Your Earn and Save Bonus eligibility will be automatically assessed

**Self-employed persons**

- Declare your income to IRAS to be assessed for Earn and Save Bonus

title: Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)
description: A legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.

sections.About this support: An LPA allows you to appoint trusted individuals to make decisions on (i) personal welfare and (ii) property and affairs, on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.
sections.Who is this for?:
Donors must:

- Be 21 years old and above
- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions
- Not be an undischarged bankrupt if you wish to make an LPA for property and affairs matters

Donees must:

- Be 21 years old and above
- Be your spouse or partner, family member or relative, friend, or a licensed trust company for property and affair matters only
- Have the mental capacity to make their own decisions
sections.How to apply?:
You can:

- [Apply online](https://opg-eservice.msf.gov.sg/) or
- You may also [book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance
  for your application. Please note that a [LPA certificate issuer](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa) is required to ensure that the donor has the mental capacity to make a LPA.
sections.What to expect?:
Here are the steps on how to make an LPA:

- Step 1: Decide on the type of LPA form
  - LPA Form 1 grants general powers to Donee(s) who will make decisions on your behalf when you lose mental capacity
  - LPA Form 2 is for applicants who want to appoint more than 2 Donees and/or more than 1 replacement Donee, and grant specific or customised powers that are not in the scope of LPA Form 1. You will need to engage a lawyer for LPA Form 2.
- Step 2: [Find an LPA certificate issuer ](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa)who is:
  - A medical professional accredited by the OPG
  - A registered psychiatrist
  - A practising lawyer (excluding lawyers registered under section 36E of the Legal Profession Act 1966)
- You and the LPA certificate issuer must digitally sign the LPA using the Singpass app. Your Donees can sign electronically by accepting their appointment.
- For your LPA to be legally valid, the certificate issuer must submit the LPA application to Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) via OPG Online (OPGO), as authorised by you.

title: Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)
description: Enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of children with special needs.
highlights: Parents may nominate child to receive payouts from their CPF savings after they pass on
Minimum monthly payout is $250, parents may decide on a higher amount
Submit the application and supporting documents to SNTC via email or mail

sections.About this support:
- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.
- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.
sections.Who is this for?:
The nominating applicant should be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs

The child with special needs should:

- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

**Or**

- is attending or had attended a Special Education School

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around
sections.How to apply?:
Before proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.

Find out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification

You can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:

- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824
- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

You'll need to provide copies of:

- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC
- Child's Birth Certificate

If your child's disability status has not been verified:

- Supporting document from the SPED school issued on the school’s official letterhead stating that the Person with Special Needs (PSN) is currently attending or has previously attended the SPED school or
- [Disability Verification Form (DVF) ](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)completed by a Registered Healthcare Professional*

After mailing the application and upon approval by MSF, parents will receive an eligibility letter, which they should bring to the CPF Board to make the SNSS nomination.

*Please note that a submitted Disability Verification Form (DVF) does not mean that your child’s disability status has been verified.

[22 Lengkok Bahru 159824](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159824)

Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable,

Enabling Village #03-03

[6278 9598](tel:62789598)

(Operating hours: 9am-6pm on weekdays, closed on weekends and public holidays)

title: Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme
description: Boost your own or loved ones’ retirement savings and payouts through voluntary cash top-ups or CPF transfer to your own or loved ones' Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA).
highlights: Boost CPF retirement savings and monthly payouts
Earn interest rates of up to 6% per annum on retirement savings
Tax relief of up to $16,000 for cash top-ups

sections.About this support:
- Receive higher monthly payouts in retirement
- Earn CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum on retirement savings
- Grow your retirement savings through the power of compound interest for higher monthly payouts
- Enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 for cash top-ups made to your own and loved ones' retirement savings each calendar year
- Find out more on the [conditions to qualify for tax relief](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-are-the-conditions-for-me-to-enjoy-tax-relief-to-special-account-or-retirement-account)

Note:

- In keeping with the objective of the scheme, cash top-ups and CPF transfers are irreversible, and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes (e.g. for housing, investment or withdrawn for immediate needs after age 55).
- Cash top-ups that attract the MRSS matching grant do not qualify for tax relief.
sections.Who is this for?:
- You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident to receive cash top-ups and CPF transfers
- You can check your top-up limits by logging in to your [Retirement Dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/ds/dashboards/retirement)
- Members aged 55 and above can top up to the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)
  - The ERS increases each year so you can top up more each year
- Members below 55 can top up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS)
- CPF transfers can be made to yourself or your loved ones:

CPF transfer to
Remarks
Yourself
You can transfer your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to your SA if you are below 55. 

If you are aged 55 or above, you can transfer your OA savings to your RA. 

How much you can transfer depends on your age and CPF balances.
Loved ones 
(parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, spouse and siblings)
Before transferring your CPF savings to your loved ones, you must first set aside enough for your own retirement. 

The amount of CPF transfers you can make to them depends on how much your loved one can receive, and the amount you can transfer.

- For more information on your [eligibility for cash transfers, CPF top-ups etc., please refer here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/saving-more-with-cpf/top-up-to-enjoy-higher-retirement-payouts)
sections.How to apply?:
- You can make your cash top-up or CPF transfer [online](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/cash-top-ups-and-cpf-transfers-for-retirement) (CPF transfers and cash top-ups via PayNow or GIRO) or via the CPF Mobile app (CPF transfers and cash tops-ups via PayNow)
- To complete your top-up form, you will need:
  - your recipient’s NRIC, if making a cash top-up or CPF transfer to a loved one
  - additional supporting documents if making a CPF transfer to a recipient for the first time (not required for cash top-ups)
- For more information on the application process, please refer [here.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-to-make-a-top-up)
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only
sections.Phone number:
CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: Legal Aid Bureau
description: Provides legal help for eligible individuals in various civil proceedings.
highlights: Legal representation for qualified applicants in various civil proceedings
Assistance with drafting Wills and Deeds of Separation
Free Legal advice for qualified applicants in various civil proceedings

sections.About this support:
- Legal advice on Singapore law and practical steps for your case.
- Assistance in drafting simple legal documents like Wills and Deeds of Separation.
- Legal representation in various civil proceedings, subject to eligibility.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents residing in Singapore

Eligibility Tests:

- Means Test for Legal Advice and Assistance
- Means and Merits Test for Legal Aid
- Duty Lawyer available for consultation and assessment of eligibility for legal aid.
sections.How to apply?:
- Register case [online](https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/labesvc/) with the [step by step guide](https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/files/AP_Portal_Guide_09032026.pdf) on the [Applicant Portal](https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/labesvc/?tabIndex=3)
- Attend the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) within three working days after online registration
- Schedule an appointment via the [OneMinLaw Portal](https://go.gov.sg/omp) before visiting the Minlaw Services Centre at 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, the URA Centre (East Wing)
- If you're a minor or representing someone without mental incapacity, a parent/guardian, or Court-appointed Deputy must apply on your behalf respectively.
sections.Where to go: [45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=069118)

title: CPF Nomination
description: Allows you to decide what happens to your CPF savings after your death.

sections.About this support:
A CPF nomination allows you to decide:

- Who will receive your CPF savings (your “nominee”)
- The percentage of your CPF savings each nominee should receive
- CPF savings **cannot be distributed by a will **as CPF savings do not form part of your estate. This arrangement **protects your CPF savings from creditor claims** on any outstanding debts you may have and preserves your savings fully for your nominees.

Your CPF nomination will cover:

- CPF savings in your Ordinary, Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts
- CPF LIFE premium balance
- Your discounted Singtel shares (if any)

Your CPF nomination does not cover:

- Properties bought using your CPF savings
- Payout from the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS)
- Investments under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)
sections.Who is this for?:
To make a CPF nomination, you must:

- Be a CPF member
- Be aged 16 years and above
- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions

You can **nominate any person or legal entity*** to be the beneficiary of your CPF savings.

*An entity that is capable of receiving monies in its own right.
sections.How to apply?:
You can:

- Apply [online](http://cpf.gov.sg/MakeCPFNOM) using your Singpass
- [Make an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form) to apply in person at any CPF service centre if you are unable to find two witnesses
- [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) to visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) for in-person guidance on your online nomination application. Click [here](https://www.psd.gov.sg/servicesg/) for the list of ServiceSG Centres and their operating hours

**For online application**

You will need to have:

**Your nominees’ particulars**

1. Full Name
2. NRIC or Foreign Identification Number (FIN)
3. Mailing Address (for foreigners)
4. Email Address (optional)

**Two witnesses’ particulars**

1. Full Name
2. NRIC
3. Email address and/or Singapore-registered mobile phone number
4. Cannot be a nominee
5. He/she cannot be a nominee and must be at least 21 years of age

Upon submission of your nomination,** inform your witnesses to log in **[here](http://cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM)** within 7 calendar days to witness your nomination using their Singpass.**

**For in-person application**

You will need to bring along and prepare:

- A copy of your NRIC/passport
- Your nominee(s)' NRIC number or Foreign Identification Number (FIN), email (optional), and mailing address (for foreigners)

As CPF Board's customer service executives or ServiceSG staff are acting as your witnesses, you do not need to prepare your witnesses' particulars.
sections.What to expect?:
If your nominee falls into the following categories, here is what to expect:

**Below 18 Years Old**
The monies will be held in trust by the Public Trustee until your nominee turns 18.
**Unable To Make Decisions Independently**
The monies will be handled by their court appointed deputy.
**Bankrupt**
The monies belonging to the undischarged bankrupt nominee, will be transferred to the Official Assignee.

To allow your CPF savings to be distributed swiftly according to your wishes when you pass on, it is important to **review your CPF nomination regularly**, especially at key milestones (e.g.):

- Starting Work
- Marriage*
- Childbirth
- Divorce
- Death of a nominee
- When you reach your golden years**

*Your nomination will be revoked upon marriage, and you should make a new nomination.

**Review your nomination and consider your current family circumstances, such as which family member may need your savings more.

title: Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme
description: Supplements eligible workers' income and CPF savings through cash and CPF payments.
highlights: Eligible employees, platform workers and self-employed persons can receive cash and CPF payments to supplement their income and grow their CPF savings for retirement, housing and healthcare
Employees can receive up to $4,900 per year
Self-employed persons and Platform Workers can receive up to $3,267 per year

sections.About this support:
**Employees**

- From Work Year 2025, eligible recipients will receive monthly payments of up to $4,900 per year, comprising 40% in cash and 60% credited to CPF Accounts

**Self-employed persons and Platform Workers**

- From Work Year 2025, eligible recipients will receive annual payments of up to $3,267, comprising 10% cash and 90% credited to MediSave Account
- Self-employed persons will receive payments annually, while Platform Workers will receive payments monthly
- From Work Year 2029, eligible Platform Workers whose CPF contribution rates fully align with that of employees will receive higher WIS payments at the same level as employees
sections.Who is this for?:
**Eligibility criteria**

- 30 years old and above as at 31 December of the Work Year
- Singapore Citizen
- Employee, self-employed person and/or platform worker
- Gross monthly income of $500* to $3,000 (if married, assessable income of recipient's spouse must not exceed $70,000), for the month worked
- Average gross monthly income of not more than S$3,000 in the past 12 months as an employee or platform worker
- Annual value of the place of residence (as indicated on NRIC) must not exceed $21,000, as at 31 December of the preceding year
- Does not own more than 1 property (if married, recipient and spouse must not own more than 1 property)

*Persons with disabilities, workers who qualify for ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance and caregivers of care recipients (generally include caregivers residing with care recipients who are medically certified to have permanent moderate to severe disabilities) will qualify for concessionary WIS, even if they earn less than $500.
sections.How to apply?:
**Employees**

- No application required
- Your WIS eligibility will be automatically assessed based on the income declared by your employer(s) for work done in that month

**Self-employed persons**

- Declare your net trade income to IRAS and make the required MediSave contributions in full

**Platform workers**

- No application required
- Your WIS eligibility will be automatically assessed based on the net earnings declared by your platform operator(s) for work done in that month
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only
sections.Phone number:
CPFB Hotline: [1800 227 1188](tel:1800-2271188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: Lease Buyback Scheme
description: Provides seniors with a steady stream of retirement income when they sell the tail-end of their flat lease to HDB while they continue to occupy the flat for the lease they retained.
highlights: Receive monthly payouts and continue to stay in the flat for the lease retained when you sell the tail-end lease of your flat to HDB
Application takes about 3 months to complete from the date of interest to proceed
Make an e-appointment with HDB for a preliminary financial counselling session

sections.About this support:
- Sell part of your flat's lease to HDB and choose to retain the length of lease based on the age of the youngest owner
- Proceeds from selling part of your flat's lease will be used to top up your CPF Retirement Account (RA), and you can use your CPF RA to join CPF LIFE, which will provide you with a monthly income for life
sections.Who is this for?:
- At least 1 owner must be a Singapore Citizen
- All owners 65 years and older
- Monthly household income not more than $14,000
- No concurrent ownership of second property, and no more than 1 non-residential private property
- All owners have been living in the flat for at least 5 years, or 10 years for Plus or Prime flats
- Flat has at least 20 years of lease to sell to HDB
sections.How to apply?:
- Learn about your eligibility for this scheme (and other housing monetisation options) and the estimated monthly payouts you can receive via [HDB’s 'Check Housing Monetisation Option' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR05AWEnquireHMOptions)
- To apply:
  - Make an [appointment](http://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BF13AWAppointmentWeb/branch) with an HDB Branch office
  - Log in with or without Singpass
  - Click on 'Make a new appointment'
  - Select 'Lease Buyback Scheme'
  - Then 'Enquiry'

title: Application for Deceased's Unnominated CPF Monies
description: Distribution of the un-nominated Central Provident Fund (CPF) monies of the Deceased Member in accordance with the relevant written law.
highlights: CPF money of the deceased without a valid nomination is forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for administration

sections.About this support:
- The un-nominated Central Provident Fund (CPF) monies of the Deceased Member can be distributed according to the applicable intestacy laws.
- If the beneficiaries include minors, the Public Trustee’s Office can hold the money in trust for them until they reach the maturity age of 21 years old.
sections.Who is this for?: Next-of-kin of deceased CPF member who wish to make a claim.
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply online via the “Deceased’s un-nominated CPF / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA” option at [Public Trustee's Office (PTO) E-Services](https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/pto) using your Singpass.
  If you are ineligible to apply for a Singpass, you may apply for a login ID and password [here](https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/pto). Select 'Login' and choose 'Register as Individual' from the dropdown menu.

- Please refer to [Annex A](https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/Information_Page/AnnexA_Muslims_Oct20.pdf) (for Muslims) and [Annex B](https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/Information_Page/AnnexB_NonMuslims_Oct20.pdf) (for non-Muslims) for documents required.
  - If the deceased was a Muslim, you will need to apply for the Certificate of inheritance via [Syariah Court ](http://www.syariahcourt.gov.sg).

title: Withdrawal of CPF Savings on Reduced Life Expectancy
description: Members with reduced life expectancy due to a medical condition, as certified by an accredited doctor (from public hospitals, polyclinics, or a specialist), may apply to withdraw some of their CPF savings. Severe medical conditions causing them to be permanently unfit for work or to lack mental capacity permanently can also be considered.
highlights: Withdraw $5,000 or more, depending on extent of your reduced life expectancy
Lump sum as well as monthly payouts from your Retirement Account, if applicable
Apply via CPF e-service and approach the Medical Institution to complete the Medical Assessment Report

sections.About this support:
- Depending on the extent of your reduced life expectancy and your CPF balances, you may withdraw a lump sum of $5,000^ or more
- You may also need to set aside a reduced retirement sum in your Retirement Account (RA), from which you will receive monthly payouts

^ Excludes monies received under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme, government grants and your MediSave Account savings.
sections.Who is this for?:
Singapore Citizen (SC) and Permanent Resident (PR) who have any of the following conditions as certified by an accredited doctor:

- Severely reduced life expectancy due to medical condition
- Permanently unfit for work
- Permanently lack mental capacity to make decisions, as defined in the Mental Capacity Act
sections.How to apply?:
**Applying for self**

- Submit [an online application](https://cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/withdraw-cpf-due-to-reduced-life-expectancy-and-claim-insurance) after logging in with your Singpass

- Download the form “Medical Assessment Report” that is provided upon submission of the online application and have it completed by an [accredited doctor](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/who-is-considered-an-accredited-doctor). Thereafter, please request the medical institution to submit the completed medical assessment report to CPF Board directly (instructions are provided within the form).
- If you are mailing your documents from overseas, all documents must be witnessed/certified true by an official of a Singapore Overseas Mission with his official seal/stamp duly affixed.

**Applying as a donee or deputy for your next-of-kin**

Submit [this form](http://cpf.gov.sg/applyrlehpsdps) with a copy of your NRIC attached and provide the following original documents to CPF Board:

- Medical report from an [accredited doctor](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/who-is-considered-an-accredited-doctor) stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;

- Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order; and

- Statement for the bank account held on trust on behalf of the member.

Make [an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us) to visit any of our CPF Service Centres to submit the above original documents or mail them to:

CPF Board 
Retirement Withdrawals Department (RWD) 
Privy Box No. 920651

Singapore 929292

title: Withdrawal of CPF Savings for Immediate Needs from Age 55
description: CPF members can make withdrawals from their CPF savings starting from age 55.
highlights: CPF members can make withdrawals from their CPF savings starting from age 55
Generally, members who turn 55 can withdraw at least $5,000 or any amount in excess after setting aside their Full Retirement Sum (FRS)
Members who own an eligible property have the flexibility to set aside their FRS with a mixture of property and cash, and withdraw their Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum

sections.About this support:
- Generally, upon turning 55, members can withdraw at least $5,000 or any amount in excess after setting aside their Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
- Members born in 1958 and after can withdraw an additional amount of up to 20% of their retirement savings when they turn 65.
- Property owners with remaining lease that lasts them until age 95 or older, have the flexibility to set aside their FRS with a mixture of property (up to half the FRS, which is half the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS)) and cash, and withdraw their Retirement Account savings above their BRS.
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents aged 55 and above.
sections.How to apply?: You may apply online via the [CPF website.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/how-to-make-cpf-withdrawal-after-55)

title: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
description: Helps eligible Singaporeans with lower retirement savings to save more by matching cash top-ups made to their Retirement or Special Accounts (RA/SA). This will boost their monthly payouts in retirement.
highlights: Dollar-for-dollar matching grant on cash top-ups to your RA/SA of up to $2,000 per year
Boost CPF retirement savings and monthly payouts
Earn CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum on cash top-ups

sections.About this support:
- The Government will match every dollar of cash top-ups made to the RA/SA of eligible Singaporeans of up to $2,000 per year, with a $20,000 cap over an eligible member’s lifetime
- The matching grant will automatically be credited to the RA/SA of the eligible member at the beginning of the following year
- Eligible Singaporeans will enjoy [interest rates of up to 6% per annum](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/earning-attractive-interest) on the cash top-up and matching grant, enhancing their retirement payouts
- Cash top-ups that attract the MRSS matching grant will not qualify for tax relief
sections.Who is this for?:
- You must meet the following criteria to be eligible:
  - Singapore Citizens only
  - Aged 55 and above as of 31st December of the assessment year, Or below 55 years old with disability status verified with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)
  - Your Retirement Account (RA) savings^ or Ordinary and Special Account (OSA) savings are less than $110,200^^
  - Average monthly income not more than $4,000
  - Annual Value of Residence not more than $21,000
  - Owns not more than 1 property
- Your eligibility for the scheme is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year, and you do not need to apply
- You can check your eligibility via your [Retirement Dashboard](http://cpf.gov.sg/retirementdashboard)

RA savings refers to the RA balances (excluding amounts such as interest earned), plus retirement withdrawals and CPF LIFE premium deducted. If you are below 55 or turning 55 in the assessment year and your RA has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.

^^ Current Basic Retirement Sum for 2026.
sections.How to apply?:
- You do not need to apply as your[ eligibility](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/who-is-eligible-for-the-matched-retirement-savings-scheme) is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year
- If you are eligible, CPF Board will notify you via email or post. You can check your eligibility via your [Retirement Dashboard](http://cpf.gov.sg/retirementdashboard)
- To [receive the matching grant](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-conditions-must-i-meet-in-order-to-receive-and-retain-the-matching-grant) you need to receive cash top-ups in your RA/SA , within the year that you are eligible for MRSS
- You can make a cash top-up [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/cash-top-ups-and-cpf-transfers-for-retirement)

title: Advance Care Planning (ACP)
description: Helps communicate your values and how they shape your healthcare preferences to your loved ones and healthcare team.

sections.About this support:
Advance Care Planning (ACP) is an ongoing process of planning and preparing for your future health and personal care. It includes conversations about your:

- personal beliefs
- values
- healthcare preferences

These will be shared with your loved ones and healthcare team.

Having a quality ACP ensures that this process is person-centred, informed and guided. In the event that you lose the capacity to make decisions or speak for yourself, the ACP will help your loved ones and healthcare team act in your best interests based on your prior expressed wishes.
sections.Who is this for?:
- For any individuals aged 21 years old* and above who has the capacity to make their own decisions.
- Includes people who are healthy and living with chronic or any other medical conditions.

ACP is particularly important for people who are living with a health condition. You can consult your regular doctor, especially if you have chronic conditions (e.g. diabetes, heart disease, chronic kidney disease) or any other medical concerns.

*For individuals below 21 years old and living with a health condition, please approach your healthcare team if you are interested to find out more about ACP.
sections.How to apply?:
You can:

1. Use the [myACP online service](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/acp/)

Complete your ACP without having to speak to an ACP facilitator. You can use the [myACP online service](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/acp/) if you:

- have a Singpass account
- are at least 21 years old
- do not have any existing serious illness
- do not have a Preferred Plan of Care (PPC) ACP or Disease Specific (DS) ACP

Once you’ve completed the online form, your NHS will receive digital invitations. They’ll be notified via SMS, and must accept or reject their appointment by logging in to My Legacy with their Singpass. Your ACP will automatically be registered once all your NHS have accepted their appointments.

1. Book an appointment with an ACP facilitator

[Visit an ACP service provider](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/listing/acp-providers/results) if you:

- prefer to have a conversation with an ACP facilitator and be guided
- have an existing serious illness*

Your ACP will be registered in the National Electronic Health Records (NEHR) upon completing all discussions with your facilitator. Some service providers may charge a nominal fee. Please check with the respective organisation for details.

* Serious illnesses include: Cancer, Stroke, End Stage Renal Failure (ESRF), Severe Liver Disease, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), Dementia, and Chronic Neurological Disease.

1. [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance for your application.

You may also refer to [this website](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/end-of-life-planning/advance-care-planning/) for more information on steps to prepare your ACP.
sections.What to expect?:
- You will need to appoint a Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS) who is responsible for speaking on your behalf about your healthcare preferences when you are no longer able to do so. In such situations, the healthcare team will consult your NHS and discuss your care plan.
- After completing your ACP, it will be available on the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR), where your healthcare team can access and refer to your ACP to prepare your care plan.

title: Matched MediSave Scheme
description: Helps eligible Singapore Citizens to strengthen MediSave adequacy by matching cash top-ups made to their MediSave Accounts (MA).
highlights: Dollar-for-dollar matching grant on cash top-ups to your MA of up to $1,000 per year
Build MA savings to help pay approved medical expenses and insurance premiums, e.g. for MediShield Life
Earn risk-free CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum on cash top-ups and matching grant

sections.About this support:
- The Government will match every dollar of cash top-ups made to the MA of eligible beneficiaries, up to $1,000 per year, starting from January 2026, for a period of five years

- The matching grant will automatically be credited to the MA of the eligible member at the beginning of the following year, i.e. from 2027

- Eligible beneficiaries will enjoy interest rates of up to 6% per annum on the cash top-ups and matching grant

- Cash top-ups that attract the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant will not qualify for tax relief
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen
- Between 55 and 70 (inclusive) as of 31 December of the year
- Does not own more than 1 property
- Annual Value of residence not more than $21,000
- Average monthly income not more than $4,000
- MA balance less than half the current Basic Healthcare Sum
sections.How to apply?:
- No application is required
- Eligibility is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year, starting from January 2026
  - If you are eligible, CPF Board will notify you via email or post
  - To receive the matching grant, you need to [receive cash top-ups in your MA](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/topupmedisave) within the year that you are eligible for Matched MediSave Scheme

title: Deputyship
description: For persons who lack mental capacity and have not made a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and/or have no donee to make certain decisions on their behalf.

sections.About this support:
- Deputyship is required if a person has lost mental capacity and did not appoint a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)
- A deputy may be the patient's family member or friend
sections.Who is this for?: Persons who have been certified to have no mental capacity.
sections.How to apply?: [Find out more on how to apply for a deputyship](https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship)
sections.What to expect?:
- You may apply to the court to seek a court order to be appointed as a Deputy.
- Anyone above 21 years of age can apply to be a Deputy. A Deputy is usually a family member or close friend who would act in the best interest of the person who lacks capacity.
- A doctor has to certify that the patient lacks mental capacity to make decisions due to an impairment of or disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain
- The Family Courts hear all deputyship applications under the Mental Capacity Act
- Applicants may need to fulfil the services’ in-take criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any.

title: Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme
description: The scheme serves individuals who may not have suitable family members or friends to appoint as their proxy decision makers. Professionals may be appointed as proxy decision makers for these individuals for remuneration.
highlights: Professional deputies have to pass a certification course and a list of stringent criteria (e.g.  no history of bankruptcy or criminal proceedings related to financial dishonesty) before they can be registered
The professional deputies have to re-register every 2 years with the Office of the Public Guardian to ensure they still meet the stringent criteria
The charges of the Professional Deputies vary depending on their professions and individual case requirements. Individuals may engage them to mutually agree on the fee charge

sections.About this support:
- Professionals registered under this scheme include lawyers, doctors, accountants, allied health professionals, nurses, and social workers
- Professional deputies apply to Court to act for individuals who lack mental capacity (known as 'P') on property &, affairs, and personal welfare matters
- Professional deputies provide a (i) P-focused plan and a (ii) Schedule of Assets as part of the application
sections.Who is this for?:
- Persons who lack mental capacity (known as ‘P’) who do not have suitable family members or friends to be their proxy decision makers
- Individuals with mental capacity can also choose to make a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), and appoint a Professional Deputy to act as a Donee for renumeration
sections.How to apply?: Members of the public who are keen to appoint a professional deputy/donee can approach any of the individuals on this [list of Registered Professional Deputies/Donees](https://www.msf.gov.sg/docs/default-source/opg/list_of_registered_professional_deputies.pdf?sfvrsn=83247f26_98) to enquire on their professional fees and to make an appointment.

title: My Legacy
description: Plan, store and share your legal, healthcare and estate matters securely with people you trust.

sections.About this support:
- My Legacy is a trusted digital companion that makes planning easy and convenient.
- It uses technology to make it seamless to document and share your plans, so that you and your loved ones can spend the time focusing on the things that matter: celebrating your relationships, achieving your life goals, and leaving a lasting legacy.
sections.Who is this for?: - Individuals aged 30 and above who are interested to find out how they can start their legacy planning.
sections.How to apply?:

sections.What to expect?:

title: Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS)
description: Provides tax relief to encourage individuals to save for retirement, over and above their CPF savings. Investment returns are tax-free before withdrawal and only 50% of withdrawals are taxable at retirement.
highlights: 50% tax concession on withdrawals from SRS at retirement
Tax relief on SRS contributions

sections.About this support:
- Provides equivalent tax relief on contributions to SRS, capped at $15,300 for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and $35,700 for foreigners
- Investment returns on SRS contributions are tax-free before withdrawal, and only 50% of withdrawals will be taxable at retirement
sections.Who is this for?:
- You can only have 1 SRS account at any point in time
- To open an SRS account, you must:
  - be at least 18 years old.
  - not be an undischarged bankrupt.
  - have the mental capacity to make own decisions
  - not have an existing SRS account (including suspended accounts) with the same or another operator
  - not have a pending application with another SRS operator.
  - not have a previous SRS account with all its funds withdrawn, on medical grounds or after reaching the prevailing retirement age (at time of your first contribution)
- To qualify for SRS Tax Relief:
  - You must be a tax resident for the Year of Assessment following the year of SRS contribution
  - Your SRS account was not suspended on 31 Dec of the year of contribution
  - You did not withdraw, from your SRS account, the same amount as you contributed in the same year of contribution
- Please note that the following conditions / criteria apply to SRS withdrawals:
  - SRS withdrawals can be made anytime. Withdrawals can be made in cash or in the form of investments
  - Withdrawals are subject to income tax (based on the time and circumstances of withdrawal) and will be considered part of your taxable income
  - Foreigners and Permanent Residents who make withdrawals are subject to withholding tax
  - Withdrawals made before retirement age will be subject to penalties unless they were made due to exceptional circumstances.

You may read up on the additional criteria and details on [SRS withdrawals and the relevant taxes here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/tax-on-srs-withdrawals).
sections.How to apply?:
- To open an SRS account:
  - Choose 1 of 3 SRS operators (DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) Ltd, United Overseas Bank (UOB) Ltd.) to set up an SRS account with
  - Tax relief will be provided automatically, if eligible
- For foreigners:
  - You must complete the [SRS Declaration Form](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/doc/annual-declaration-form-for-supplementary-retirement-scheme.doc?sfvrsn=e34e4cdd_22)

Note: You must update your SRS bank operator if you become a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, even if you have already contributed this year, as your maximum contribution amount will have to be recalculated and may be pro-rated.
